NASA FIRMS standard archive · 2003–2025 · Local time in Punjab

Method and sources

The analysis uses NASA FIRMS standard-quality detections from Aqua MODIS (2003–2025), Suomi NPP VIIRS (2016–2025), and NOAA‑20 VIIRS (2018–2025). It applies each platform’s native daytime vegetation quality filters. One active cell-day counts one 10 km equal-area cell with at least one qualifying report on a local date. The 11 seven-day windows span 15 September to 30 November.

The district geometry is the geoBoundaries snapshot. Each grid cell is assigned to the district with its largest Punjab-clipped overlap. Border cells may contain reports on either side. All years use those same assignments. The statewide view includes all Punjab cells.

The regional model uses the median annual Aqua-to-VIIRS ratio. Pooled seasonal factors blend three phases with the area-wide factor. Calibration uses 2016–2021 for Suomi NPP and 2018–2021 for NOAA‑20. The holdout uses 2022–2025. The district transfer row excludes the selected district’s cells from fitting. Historical P90 is the 90th percentile for the selected area and seven-day window in the 2003–2021 Aqua archive.

Sensor agreement is the number of cell-days with reports from both platforms divided by the number with a report from either. It measures co-reporting. Granule footprints show approximate published geometry for three case weeks. Clear-sky coverage remains unverified. NASA/LANCE FIRMS and NASA Earthdata CMR supply the data. geoBoundaries supplies boundaries under its published license.
